top.title: FCTA upgrades 20 PHCs, says pregnant women to get ambulance in 4 mins
top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Capital Territory Administration FCTA has upgraded 20 primary health centres across the territory, declaring that it has cut emergency ambulance response to pregnant women to less than four minutes. Mandate Secretary, FCT Health Services and Environment Secretariat, Dr Adedolapo Fasawe, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja at the community engagement and inauguration of the renovated and upgraded Owner-Occupier Model Primary Health Centre PHC, Kubwa. She said the upgrade was carried out under the World Bank-supported Immunisation Plus and Malaria Progress by Accelerating Coverage and Transforming Services IMPACT project. To demonstrate how the emergency system works, Fasawe asked a pregnant woman to call one of the emergency lines. The ambulance reached the scene in less than four minutes. She said emergency response had been strengthened through the FCT Emergency Medical Services and Ambulance System (FEMSAS), which operates 24 hours a day, is free of charge, and brings local transport operators into the system to convey pregnant women during emergencies. According to her, the intervention goes beyond physical renovation. The administration has also built staff accommodation, provided modern medical equipment and installed solar-powered systems to guarantee 24-hour electricity and round-the-clock service. “The PHC is usually the first port of call for most residents. This is fundamental to improving health outcomes, reducing preventable deaths, and achieving universal health coverage. “This is just one of 20 primary healthcare centres across different communities in the FCT that were upgraded under the IMPACT project,” she added. On affordability, she said at least 1,000 vulnerable residents were being registered free of charge on the spot into the FCT Health Insurance Scheme under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund. The enrolment, she explained, entitles them to one year of free medical care in accredited public and private hospitals. Fasawe also commended the Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, for road construction and rehabilitation projects across the satellite towns, which she said had drastically reduced travel time to health facilities. She said the administration’s healthcare intervention rests on three pillars, which are access, affordability and quality, in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu. Fasawe urged traditional rulers and community leaders to take ownership of the upgraded facilities, monitor service delivery and make sure patients are not charged for free services. “Healthcare should not be a luxury reserved for a few. Quality healthcare is your fundamental human right,” she said. The Executive Secretary of the FCT Primary Health Care Board, Dr Dan Gadzama, said the Federal Government initiative began in 2021 with an initial completion date of December 2025. top.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' gets final trailer, explaining why Steve Rogers is back and showing an epic battle with the X-Men
top.description: The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday just landed, and it finally puts the spotlight on our boy Steve Rogers. Avengers: Doomsday has been promising the scale and excitement the MCU has often been lacking since the Infinity Saga. Previous trailers played it safe, mostly setting up the conflict and introducing Victor Von Doom. Now it’s time for one last explosive look at the film before it tries to conquer cinemas next month. Disney and Marvel Studios have just released a “final trailer” that puts the focus back on Steve Rogers — no longer Captain America but still ready to use Mjolnir — and Thor as the veterans leading the New Avengers, former colleagues, the Fantastic Four, and even Fox’s X-Men (after some first-encounter fights, of course) against Doom and his followers. A few dodgy CG shots aside, it looks grand, and if you’re a big X-Men fan, it’s hard not to get goosebumps when Cyclops (James Marsden) finally gets to say the thing. The multiverse-spanning story is still largely kept a secret in this trailer, but at least we get a better sense of what the emotional stakes are for Rogers and how all these heroes can realistically work together against the greatest threat they’ve faced so far (even if most of them won’t get more than a few lines). (Image credit: Marvel) As for Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom, this isn’t his trailer, but the mysterious Latverian witches — who have fueled many theories online for months — are finally seen in motion. Doom has, however, received a simple but evocative poster that mirrors one of the original Iron Man ones. Even though Marvel Studios' honcho, Kevin Feige, has shot down the theory that this Victor Von Doom is a Tony Stark variant , you can’t stop marketing from doing the obvious things, it seems. We won’t complain. (Image credit: Marvel Studios) Avengers: Doomsday won’t fix all of the Multiverse Saga’s shortcomings, but at the very least, it looks like a proper fun time with more toys being mashed together than ever before and proper stakes. Right before Christmas, it’s hard to resist such a pitch. Avengers: Doomsday assembles on December 18, 2026, only in cinemas...Yes, it opens the same day as Dune: Part Three . top.title: Democrats fire starting gun on 2028 White House race
top.description: Democrats fired the starting gun Monday on the race to win back the White House, announcing plans for 12 debates to pick their standard bearer for 2028 as the party looks to build on its sweeping midterm election victory. The first debate is scheduled for June next year, setting the stage for what could be a crowded contest to select a challenger to the Republicans, who must find a successor to term-limited President Donald Trump. The announcement comes as Democrats celebrate their biggest majority in the House of Representatives since the early 1990s, with their victories this month transforming the balance of power in Washington and raising expectations for the next two years. “Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” Democratic National Committee chairman Ken Martin said. The party will hold five debates in 2027 and seven in 2028, the final one scheduled for March of that year. The debates will help voters choose the party’s presidential nominee through a series of state-by-state primary elections and caucuses, in which supporters select the candidate they want to face the Republican nominee in November 2028. Under new rules announced Monday, candidates seeking a place on the debate stage must pledge to denounce spending on their behalf by outside political groups, including those that do not disclose their donors. The requirement is intended to curb the influence of wealthy donors and so-called “dark money” in Democratic nomination contests, a longstanding demand of the party’s progressive wing. With a potentially large field, some debates could be spread across two nights, with a maximum of 20 candidates participating. No major Democrat has formally entered the race, but maneuvering is already underway among politicians seeking to become the party’s standard-bearer. Gavin Newsom, Josh Shapiro and Andy Beshear — the governors of California, Pennsylvania and Kentucky, respectively — are among those attracting attention as possible contenders. top.title: British retailer Next downplays data breach at tech supplier
top.description: British retailer Next has become the latest high street name to find itself caught up in a cyberattack, although it insists the data accessed by hackers is "benign" and its customers have nothing to worry about. The clothing and homeware giant told investors on Monday that a third-party supplier had suffered a security breach, allowing an unauthorized party to access information relating to Next. The retailer says its own systems remain untouched and that, so far, there's no evidence that customer personal data has fallen into the wrong hands. "We have been informed that one of our third-party online suppliers has experienced a cyber incident which has resulted in unauthorized access to certain benign data relating to NEXT," the company said in its statement, which it shared with The Register . "We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier." The breached supplier provides technology services to Next, and the "benign" information accessed is understood to be low-level data. Sensitive customer details, including addresses, passwords, and banking information, are believed to be unaffected. Next hasn't identified the supplier, explained exactly what the hackers managed to get their hands on, or revealed how much information was accessed, and declined to say when asked by The Register . However, the retailer has seemingly decided that the stolen data won’t be of much use to the criminals responsible. "Our investigations are ongoing; however, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised," Next said. "The information affected is limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or NEXT." Next also stressed that its own IT infrastructure had escaped unscathed, saying it was "confident that NEXT’s own systems have not been compromised and that this remains an incident affecting the supplier's environment." Despite repeatedly describing the compromised information as harmless, Next says it is treating the incident "with the utmost seriousness" and is working with the affected supplier, law enforcement, and relevant regulators. The incident comes just weeks after fellow British fashion retailer Asos suffered a breach of its own , with hackers gaining access to customer information through third-party platforms. That attack, which came to light on October 6 when customers received an unauthorized push notification through the Asos app announcing that the company had been hacked, was traced to a social engineering scam. An attacker impersonated a trusted contact to trick an Asos employee into handing over login credentials, which were then used to access external platforms. Asos later admitted that the intruders had accessed customer names, contact details, and some account information, but passwords and payment card details were apparently off limits. top.title: Tennessee fined $250,000 after fans threw mustard and golf balls at coach
top.description: The Southeastern Conference has fined Tennessee $250,000 after fans threw a slew of objects toward LSU and their coach Lane Kiffin during a game the Volunteers won 27-13. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey announced the penalty under the league's sportsmanship, game management and alcohol availability policies on Sunday. The trouble began with 3:14 remaining in the game when supporters in the Tennessee student section threw golf balls toward the Tigers bench. Play was halted for several minutes while the objects flew, and players gathered near the middle of the field to keep clear of any direct hits. Tennessee Volunteers fans react during the first half of the game against the LSU Tigers at Neyland Stadium on November 21, 2026 (Getty Images) “The golf balls have started being thrown at Neyland Stadium,” sports reporter Rhiannon Potkey wrote alongside video from the game. SportsCenter shared additional footage of a Tennessee staff member then carried a handful of golf balls and a mustard bottle to the sidelines. A message on the giant screen urged fans: “Keep your composure and practice good sportsmanship.” Kiffin ordered his players to exit through a side entrance once the game had finished rather than expose them to the home crowd a second time. “If cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues, the institution is subject to an immediate fine and suspension of the alcohol sales privilege," SEC rules state. The league has decided not to suspend alcohol sales at Tennessee for now, but it retains the right to do so in future. The hostility from Volunteers fans toward Kiffin stretches back to 2009, when he spent a single year as the university's head coach before leaving for USC. He came back for the first time in 2021, by then in charge of Ole Miss, and Kiffin and the Rebels were pelted with debris on that occasion too, some of it golf balls and a mustard bottle. Jeremiah Telander #22 of the Tennessee Volunteers celebrates after a 27-13 victory against the LSU (Getty Images) Tennessee students burned mattresses after Kiffin's departure, and in 2010 a Knoxville lawyer suggested renaming a wastewater treatment facility as the “Lane Kiffin Sewage Plant.” Tennessee coach Josh Heupel was asked about Kiffin's return, now as LSU head coach, during SEC media days this summer and referred back to the 2021 incident. “I certainly hope our fan base hasn’t cooled off.” Heupel said. “Whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard or our sports stores, making sure that they got reinforcements on the golf balls ... hopefully Knoxville’s ready for his arrival.” The fine is Tennessee's second in quick succession, after the SEC fined the school $500,000 a month ago for allowing fans to storm the field following a 26-10 victory over then-No. 6 Alabama. top.title: Rejoice! Luca Williams-Barnett’s assist has officially been credited on appeal!
top.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: Luca Williams-Barnett of Tottenham Hotspur during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on November 21, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images I did not realize this had happened until it was already over this morning, but apparently after Saturday’s Tottenham Hotspur win over Ipswich Town, Luca Williams-Barnett was NOT credited with a goal and an assist to Dominic Solanke — just the goal. Stat trackers Opta initially did not give the assist to Williams-Barnett as it was initially judged to have taken a very slight deflection off of Ipswich keeper Christian Walton. However, after review, Opta has officially reversed course and has issued Luca his assist, and even posted about how that made him the second youngest player to ever score and assist in a Premier League game. However, to hear him tell it, it was James Maddison who pressured Opta to begin with. After the match, Madders apparently emailed Opta to ask why Williams-Barnett didn’t get credited with the assist, and then followed up on social media to take “credit” for Opta switching gears. I’ve watched the highlights of LWB’s assist many times over the past couple of days and I have to say I had no idea it initially wasn’t granted, because it’s so obviously an assist that it never crossed my mind. So kudos to Opta for looking at the evidence and officially making Luca second to Michael Owen in a trivia category. That’s pretty heady company to be keeping, and hopefully he’ll continue to do great things while at Tottenham.

top.title: York repeats as state volleyball champion while Victor, Mercy fall short
top.description: GREIGSVILLE – York accomplished what most high school girls volleyball programs only dream of: Back-to-back state championships. The Golden Knights defeated Hamilton (Section III) in straight sets (25-15, 25-16, 25-19) Nov. 21 to win the 2026 NYSPHSAA Class D title at Harding Mazzotti Arena in Glens Falls. They received a champion’s welcome upon returning home to Livingston County. Bailey Orman was awarded most valuable player of the Class D state tournament for the second consecutive year. The junior also reached a personal milestone in Glens Falls – 1,000 career kills. A parade of fire trucks from Cuylerville, Leicester and York accompanied Orman and the Golden Knights’ return home. Dozens of fans cheered – many waving yellow towels – as they deboarded a school bus with championship plaque in hand. “We didn’t really get into a groove until the very end of the season,” York coach Kaitlin Kolb said. “We worked hard over the postseason to keep meshing together and play our roles to the best of our ability. It really came together in the finals.” Welcome home York earned its spot in the Class D final by finishing 2-1 in pool play. Despite its loss to Candor (IV), York advanced with wins over Hamilton and Duanesburg (II). JJ Kane recorded a whopping 25 digs in the championship match, adding five kills and four assists. Tessa Goodell distributed 23 assists while Bree Parsons logged 13 kills, five digs and three blocks. Orman totaled 12 kills, 10 digs and two blocks against Hamilton. CC Biondo had 11 digs, Jordan Ray added 10 digs, and Fiona Grant chipped in four kills and four digs for York. “We have a great support system,” said Parsons, a senior. “I think that’s one of the reasons we’ve gotten so far – they were always here to support us. Goodell, meanwhile, orchestrated the offense at setter, dishing out 51 assists in pool play to go with her 21 digs. Parsons and Orman each totaled 20 kills in pool play. Orman, who also had 20 digs, recorded her 1,000 th career kill. “My parents and all the people I started my career with,” Orman said, “have really helped me grow and gotten me over some challenging times.” Parsons and Goodell joined Orman on the Class D all-tournament team. Biondo won the sportsmanship award. “It still feels so unreal even though it’s the second time we’ve experienced it,” said Biondo, a senior. “Each year is so unique because we all need to learn about each other on and off the court. top.title: Rennie gets backing despite All Black defeats
top.description: Dave Rennie took the All Blacks role following the departure of Scott Robertson [Getty Images] All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has received the unequivocal backing of his bosses at New Zealand Rugby to lead the team through to next year's World Cup. Rennie's side have suffered back-to-back defeats in the November leg of the Nations Championship and have lost five times in the calendar year for the first time since 1998. "We have complete confidence in him," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change." Rennie was appointed in March and started his All Blacks tenure in style, dispatching France and Ireland in the July part of the Nations Championship before a memorable victory over world champions South Africa in the Springboks' spiritual home of Ellis Park. But New Zealand lost the next three Tests against the Boks to fall 3-1 in the 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' [RGR] series, and, although two convincing wins over Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup, the All Blacks have endured a difficult tour of Europe. A first loss to Wales in 73 years was followed by an English rout in Twickenham, while the All Blacks have also been hit by the tragic death of their long-serving head of security Logan Cadwallader. The emotional toll of Cadwaller's passing along with the arduous schedule this year are thought to be two mitigating factors behind the dip in form, and New Zealand's administrators will review the impact of the RGR series when planning its return in 2030. Lancaster added that the union will look to make a call in the middle of next year as to whether Rennie takes charge of the team beyond the 2027 World Cup. "We will conduct a full campaign and season review following this year, as we always do," he said. "That will inform how we approach next year, but it will also inform our discussions around what the contract situation looks like beyond next year. "Our intention is to make all those decisions and have clarity before we go into the World Cup. Nothing has changed from when we appointed [Rennie] earlier this year. "He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment." top.title: YouTube Star Secures Shock DP World Tour Invite
top.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images YouTube content creator Peter Finch has accepted a surprise sponsor invite to play the AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open on the DP World Tour. The event begins on December 10 and features a field that includes two-time Masters champion Bubba Watson. Finch, who runs a channel with over 850,000 subscribers, will compete against multiple tour winners in this 72-hole stroke play event. Finch announced the opportunity to his Instagram followers on Nov. 20, confirming that he will make his DP World Tour debut at the AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open. The opportunity was not entirely new: Finch had discussed receiving the sponsor exemption on his Rough Cut Golf Podcast in October. The Path to the Field Finch’s journey to the professional stage has been steady but difficult. Finch has some professional tournament experience, including a tied-50th finish at the 2025 Egyptian Open on the Asian Development Tour. He also reached Final Qualifying for The Open in 2025 and finished tied for sixth at the 2026 Fairmont St Andrews Classic on the Tartan Pro Tour. The Mauritius Open will represent a significant step up in competition. These results showed he could handle pressure, yet the DP World Tour invite remains a step up in class. The tournament field features plenty of proven talent. South African stars Branden Grace, Thriston Lawrence and Dean Burmester are multiple DP World Tour winners. Casey Jarvis, another rising South African star with multiple tour victories, will also compete. They will be joined by Bubba Watson and defending champion Jayden Schaper. Regarding the opportunity, Finch wrote on Instagram, “I cannot wait to get out to Mauritius and compete against some of the best players in the world!” He noted that he has followed the event for a long time and sees this as a major milestone. “I remember watching this tournament over the years and just thinking what an amazing spectacle and an amazing privilege it would be to play at these courses, and that’s what we’re going to be doing,” Finch added in his post. Content Creation Meets Competition This dual role as competitor and creator adds a unique layer to the tournament narrative. While other players focus solely on their scorecards, Finch will be documenting the experience for his large online audience. Finch’s documentation of the experience could bring new eyes to the DP World Tour and highlight the challenges facing the sport. Finch’s participation also highlights the growing overlap between golf’s traditional professional tours and its enormous online content community. His tournament videos could give viewers an unusual look at the pressures of competing in a DP World Tour event. With more than 851,000 YouTube subscribers, Finch could introduce the tournament to golf fans who might not otherwise follow the DP World Tour. top.description: The Kansas City Chiefs hosted the Arizona Cardinals in an important Week 11 matchup at Arrowhead Stadium, hoping to extend their winning streak to three games. The offense maintained a balanced attack, led by running back Emmett Johnson and veteran Travis Kelce, who scored twice. Patrick Mahomes spread the ball around, with Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen making plays alongside Rashee Rice at wide receiver. nigeria.title: Democrats fire starting gun on 2028 White House race
nigeria.description: Democrats fired the starting gun Monday on the race to win back the White House, announcing plans for 12 debates to pick their standard bearer for 2028 as the party looks to build on its sweeping midterm election victory. The first debate is scheduled for June next year, setting the stage for what could be a crowded contest to select a challenger to the Republicans, who must find a successor to term-limited President Donald Trump. The announcement comes as Democrats celebrate their biggest majority in the House of Representatives since the early 1990s, with their victories this month transforming the balance of power in Washington and raising expectations for the next two years. “Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” Democratic National Committee chairman Ken Martin said. The party will hold five debates in 2027 and seven in 2028, the final one scheduled for March of that year. The debates will help voters choose the party’s presidential nominee through a series of state-by-state primary elections and caucuses, in which supporters select the candidate they want to face the Republican nominee in November 2028. Under new rules announced Monday, candidates seeking a place on the debate stage must pledge to denounce spending on their behalf by outside political groups, including those that do not disclose their donors. The requirement is intended to curb the influence of wealthy donors and so-called “dark money” in Democratic nomination contests, a longstanding demand of the party’s progressive wing. With a potentially large field, some debates could be spread across two nights, with a maximum of 20 candidates participating. No major Democrat has formally entered the race, but maneuvering is already underway among politicians seeking to become the party’s standard-bearer. Gavin Newsom, Josh Shapiro and Andy Beshear — the governors of California, Pennsylvania and Kentucky, respectively — are among those attracting attention as possible contenders. He said Nigeria was already facing a dangerous combination of insecurity, political mistrust and weaknesses in the electoral system, which could create opportunities for armed non-state actors to exploit any post-election crisis. “The moment there’s a slight political crisis, the militia and terrorist groups, who are well organised, may take advantage of the political instability to expand and declare control in some states in the North and they will begin to press towards Abuja,” he said. The Accord Party candidate also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s handling of national crises, alleging that the President had repeatedly failed to remain in the country and confront challenges directly. “And President Tinubu will do the usual thing he does best, which is to run away. nigeria.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
nigeria.description: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior US government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead,” the company said in a statement. Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board. The decision came three days after Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Trump described Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions,” and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart.” Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused. Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips. US intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations. Board chair Harvey Jones said Monday that directors now believe Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers. Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who was named Nvidia’s first-ever board chair during the crisis, will stay in the role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will continue as CFO. Nvidia said a committee of independent directors set up earlier this month to investigate whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will see its probe through to the end. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said. Vanguard News The post Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Eurozone business activity still growing despite French downturn
nigeria.description: Business activity in the euro area registered a “steady” expansion this month, a key survey showed Monday, as faster growth in Germany helped counter a deepening downturn in France. The eurozone purchasing managers’ index (PMI) published by S&P Global, a gauge of the economy’s overall health, stood at 51.7 in November, unchanged from October, but below the 52.0 forecast of economists surveyed by FactSet. A reading above 50 indicates growth while one below 50 signals contraction. “At the headline level, the flash PMI data signal sustained steady growth for the eurozone in November, consistent with the economy growing at a near 0.3 percent pace in the fourth quarter,” S&P chief business economist Chris Williamson said in a statement. But he cautioned that the “overall picture of continuing economic resilience masks worrying divergences in performance within the euro area.” “While growth in Germany has accelerated to the fastest for four and a half years, as its manufacturing sector enjoys a growth spurt of the likes not seen for over five years, France is suffering a deepening downturn,” Williamson said. The German economy, he said, was benefiting strongly from “surging investment spending on defence and AI-related technologies”. At the same time, “uncertainty about the political environment, social unrest and the high cost of living are hitting service providers especially hard, especially for consumer-facing businesses, dampening growth both in France and across the rest of the region as a whole”. The European Central Bank has lifted borrowing costs twice this year in response to the energy shock triggered by the US war on Iran, and Williamson warned that “higher interest rates are also starting to show up as an increasing drag”. He noted that lower oil prices had “helped tame inflationary pressures” somewhat in November. But he predicted the PMI data alongside a “broad message” of eurozone growth would bolster calls for a further rate increase in December. nigeria.title: England launches world’s largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial
nigeria.description: England’s state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world’s largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years. The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset. The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians’ time. The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS. “This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world,” Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech’s “huge potential” while pledging “proper safeguards” to ensure safety and effectiveness. “If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery.” The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England. Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out. The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel. The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two. Recruitment has started at Cambridge University Hospitals, in eastern England, with more of the 30 selected sites opening in the coming months. Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, with around 55,000 diagnosed every year in the UK. Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for screening every three years, amounting to around 2.1 million screenings annually. The NHS estimates this helps prevent around 1,300 deaths. A study published in The Lancet medical journal in January said that AI can improve breast cancer detection through more effective screening while reducing radiologists’ workloads. It analysed nearly 106,000 mammograms performed in Sweden as part of its national breast cancer screening programme — involving women with a median age of 53 — from April 2021 to early December 2022. business.title: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed and patched a medium-severity bug that let an attacker temporarily freeze a node’s processing of blocks and transactions, a flaw first flagged by an AI scanner built by Block’s Spiral. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, is fixed in Bitcoin Core versions 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1. The 30.5 and 31.3 releases shipped Friday alongside the public advisory, while 32.1 has carried the fix since Oct. 27. Affected versions run from 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4 and 31.0 through 31.2. The 29.x series has reached end of life and will not get a fix, so operators on that branch need to move to a newer release. How the Core bug worked Bitcoin Core keeps “orphan” transactions, whose parent transactions it has not yet seen, and asks peers that announce them for the missing pieces. Since version 29.0, the software builds a list of an orphan’s parents and checks each one against its mempool and filters before deciding what to request. A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and the software did not skip duplicates. An attacker could send a node an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then send messages repeating that transaction’s ID 50,000 times. “Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks,” the advisory said. Sending more messages could stretch the disruption out. The fix makes the node process each transaction announced in an inv message only once. The advisory describes a temporary denial-of-service problem and does not describe any way to steal bitcoin or permanently damage a node. It also does not say whether the bug was ever exploited. For a business running an affected node, the stalls could still matter. An exchange could be slow to credit deposits, and a miner could keep working on an outdated view of the chain while its node is stuck. An AI-found bug under a faster disclosure policy The advisory credits an automated LLM scan run through Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral, Block’s open-source bitcoin development arm. Bitcoin Core developer Gregory Sanders validated the finding and brought it to the project’s security team. Loupe is a free scanner that runs AI agents over open-source bitcoin code and only reports findings backed by a working test case. Bitcoin Core, BDK, LDK, rust-bitcoin, Cashu, Blockstream Jade, bitcoinj and SRI signed up for its first round of scans. Rohrer said on a recent podcast that Spiral started the project around March and began continuous scanning in May, with Bitcoin Core in the first batch. Loupe reported the issue on July 8. A developer known as Stutxo independently reported it on Aug. 4, the same day Sanders opened a pull request with the fix, which was merged two days later. business.title: UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues The U.K. will bar crypto exchange operators from trading against their own capital on the venues they run, while a new Treasury order clears independent market makers to trade on those platforms without a separate dealing permission. The Financial Conduct Authority’s final rules say a firm “must not execute any orders against its proprietary capital” on a qualifying trading platform it operates. The FCA’s guidance spells out the effect: a firm “cannot act as a market maker” on its own platform. The restriction takes effect Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA rule itself is not new. The regulator published it on June 30 in policy statement PS26/11, part of a five-document package that completed its crypto rulebook. What changed last week was the Treasury’s side of the framework. What the FCA rule covers The FCA’s rulebook defines a market maker as a person who holds themselves out on a platform on a continuous basis as willing to buy and sell qualifying cryptoassets against their own capital at prices they set. That is the activity operators will be barred from on their own venues. There is one carve-out. An operator with the appropriate permission may still engage in matched principal trading to execute client orders on its platform, as long as it follows the platform’s non-discretionary rules. The FCA warned that this model does not rule out settlement risk, so firms should take steps to minimize it. The bar applies only to the operator’s own platform. Under the same rules, an operator with the right permission can still trade against its own capital outside the venue it runs. It must make clear to clients which capacity it is acting in, and it must manage conflicts of interest. Treasury clears outside market makers The Treasury made the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2026 on Nov. 18. They add a new Article 9UA to the U.K.’s crypto legislation. The article carves two kinds of activity out of the regulated activity of dealing in qualifying cryptoassets as principal. One is activity carried on “otherwise than for the purpose of providing a service to another person.” The other is activity carried on “as a market maker on a qualifying cryptoasset trading platform.” In practice, a third-party firm quoting prices on a U.K. crypto platform would not need the principal-dealing permission for that activity. The text does not say who the market maker has to be, so the bar on operators comes from the FCA’s rules rather than from the Treasury order. The explanatory note says no impact assessment was prepared because no significant new costs are expected. The FCA’s rules also put new duties on platforms that rely on market makers. American Bitcoin said the money can go toward strategic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes. “This $150 million facility provides American Bitcoin with non-dilutive capital to support our continued operations and growth initiatives,” CEO Mike Ho said in the release. Because it is revolving, the company can draw, repay and redraw funds during the term. Borrowings carry a 5.95% loan fee, plus a commitment fee on any undrawn amount. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. sports.description: The Southeastern Conference has fined Tennessee $250,000 after fans threw a slew of objects toward LSU and their coach Lane Kiffin during a game the Volunteers won 27-13. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey announced the penalty under the league's sportsmanship, game management and alcohol availability policies on Sunday. The trouble began with 3:14 remaining in the game when supporters in the Tennessee student section threw golf balls toward the Tigers bench. Play was halted for several minutes while the objects flew, and players gathered near the middle of the field to keep clear of any direct hits. Tennessee Volunteers fans react during the first half of the game against the LSU Tigers at Neyland Stadium on November 21, 2026 (Getty Images) “The golf balls have started being thrown at Neyland Stadium,” sports reporter Rhiannon Potkey wrote alongside video from the game. SportsCenter shared additional footage of a Tennessee staff member then carried a handful of golf balls and a mustard bottle to the sidelines. A message on the giant screen urged fans: “Keep your composure and practice good sportsmanship.” Kiffin ordered his players to exit through a side entrance once the game had finished rather than expose them to the home crowd a second time. “If cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues, the institution is subject to an immediate fine and suspension of the alcohol sales privilege," SEC rules state. The league has decided not to suspend alcohol sales at Tennessee for now, but it retains the right to do so in future. The hostility from Volunteers fans toward Kiffin stretches back to 2009, when he spent a single year as the university's head coach before leaving for USC. He came back for the first time in 2021, by then in charge of Ole Miss, and Kiffin and the Rebels were pelted with debris on that occasion too, some of it golf balls and a mustard bottle. Jeremiah Telander #22 of the Tennessee Volunteers celebrates after a 27-13 victory against the LSU (Getty Images) Tennessee students burned mattresses after Kiffin's departure, and in 2010 a Knoxville lawyer suggested renaming a wastewater treatment facility as the “Lane Kiffin Sewage Plant.” Tennessee coach Josh Heupel was asked about Kiffin's return, now as LSU head coach, during SEC media days this summer and referred back to the 2021 incident. “I certainly hope our fan base hasn’t cooled off.” Heupel said. “Whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard or our sports stores, making sure that they got reinforcements on the golf balls ... hopefully Knoxville’s ready for his arrival.” The fine is Tennessee's second in quick succession, after the SEC fined the school $500,000 a month ago for allowing fans to storm the field following a 26-10 victory over then-No. 6 Alabama. sports.title: Rennie gets backing despite All Black defeats
sports.description: Dave Rennie took the All Blacks role following the departure of Scott Robertson [Getty Images] All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has received the unequivocal backing of his bosses at New Zealand Rugby to lead the team through to next year's World Cup. Rennie's side have suffered back-to-back defeats in the November leg of the Nations Championship and have lost five times in the calendar year for the first time since 1998. "We have complete confidence in him," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change." Rennie was appointed in March and started his All Blacks tenure in style, dispatching France and Ireland in the July part of the Nations Championship before a memorable victory over world champions South Africa in the Springboks' spiritual home of Ellis Park. But New Zealand lost the next three Tests against the Boks to fall 3-1 in the 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' [RGR] series, and, although two convincing wins over Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup, the All Blacks have endured a difficult tour of Europe. A first loss to Wales in 73 years was followed by an English rout in Twickenham, while the All Blacks have also been hit by the tragic death of their long-serving head of security Logan Cadwallader. The emotional toll of Cadwaller's passing along with the arduous schedule this year are thought to be two mitigating factors behind the dip in form, and New Zealand's administrators will review the impact of the RGR series when planning its return in 2030. Lancaster added that the union will look to make a call in the middle of next year as to whether Rennie takes charge of the team beyond the 2027 World Cup. "We will conduct a full campaign and season review following this year, as we always do," he said. "That will inform how we approach next year, but it will also inform our discussions around what the contract situation looks like beyond next year. "Our intention is to make all those decisions and have clarity before we go into the World Cup. Nothing has changed from when we appointed [Rennie] earlier this year. "He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment." sports.title: Leaked: 1st pictures of new Arsenal home kit for 2027/28
sports.description: Leaked: 1st pictures of new Arsenal home kit for 2027/28 Arsenal’s home shirt for the 2027/28 season has leaked, with a few major changes compared to this year’s home kit. Photo via FootyHeadlines.com Footy Headlines have leaked the design of Arsenal’s home shirt for the 2027/28 season, revealing some changes from recent seasons. The main one is the use of a tonal vertical striped pattern. Arsenal have generally only used a very subtle pattern (if any) on the front of the home shirt for the last few campaigns, but this one is much more pronounced. Then there’s the change to the Emirates sponsor logo, which just reads “Emirates”, rather than including “Fly Better”. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images The shirt has also gone back to using the cannon logo, rather than the white crest on the 2025/26 and 2026/27 shirts. It also uses a v-neck collar, and there is very minor navy detailing on the collar and sleeves. Footy Headlines have revealed that the shirt will be accompanied by white shorts with red and navy trim, and red side stripes. The kit will use white socks with a dark navy hope and red ‘AFC’ lettering, and they’ve included a computer-generated mock-up of the full kit: Photo via FootyHeadlines.com As usual, the expectation is that the new kit will be released at the end of the current campaign. Whether or not it is released during the current campaign seemingly depends on whether Arsenal still have trophies to play for, as the Gunners have tended to stick with the existing shirt until the final game if they can still win something in it. If not, they’ve tended to show off the new kit in the final home game of the season. Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images For Premier League

sports.title: 'It is difficult' - Real Madrid star Thibaut Courtois admits goalkeepers face impossible Ballon d'Or battle
sports.description: Real Madrid v RC Celta de Vigo - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Thibaut Courtois has admitted he is baffled by what a goalkeeper must achieve to win the Ballon d'Or after being overlooked for the top prize in recent years. The Real Madrid number one expressed his frustration while also confirming his ultimate ambition to hang up his gloves in the Spanish capital. Frustration over individual awards Courtois has spoken candidly about the difficulties goalkeepers face in winning the Ballon d'Or , a trophy that has only been awarded to a shot-stopper once in history. Reflecting on his own career and the lack of recognition for his position, the Belgian international expressed a sense of resignation regarding the voting process. He pointed to 2022 as a year where he felt he deserved a higher ranking, noting that while Karim Benzema was a worthy winner, keepers are often relegated to the Yashin Trophy rather than the main prize. "I think I expected to be higher in 2022. Karim deserved it, but I think I should have been higher. We can perform brilliantly, but in the final minute [Kylian] Mbappe might score and that is what people will remember," explained Courtois, as quoted by AS . The veteran keeper, who recently extended his contract with the Merengues, highlighted that even standout seasons often fall short of the top individual honours. "It is difficult, I understand that, but I do not know what kind of season a goalkeeper has to have to win a Ballon d'Or. Some goalkeepers deserve to finish higher in the Ballon d'Or standings," he added. Commitment to Real Madrid Beyond his individual frustrations, Courtois made his long-term intentions clear by stating his desire to end his career at the Santiago Bernabeu. Having signed a contract extension, he emphasised that his primary goal is to remain healthy and continue winning trophies with the Spanish giants. "I'm very happy and proud to have signed for another year. My goal is to finish my career here; I need to stay healthy. I'm grateful for the club's confidence. The Champions League is tough, and with this format, everything is more open. I've won two, and I hope to win more," he confirmed. Hits back at Vinicius critics The conversation shifted to the form of Vinicius Junior, who has recently faced scrutiny for his performances . Courtois has launched a passionate defence of Vinicius, insisting that only Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are immune to dips in form. The Brazilian superstar has found himself under the microscope in recent weeks following a string of inconsistent performances for Los Blancos. However, his Belgian teammate was quick to shield him from the mounting scrutiny, reminding critics that demanding perfection every time he steps onto the pitch is an impossible standard. sports.title: Mike Breen is still chasing a better call
sports.description: Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Please don’t call Mike Breen the dean of NBA broadcasters. “This title of voice of the NBA that usually goes with whoever’s the NBA Finals announcer, I’ve never been comfortable with that,” he says. “Because I’m not the voice. There are so many voices.” Plus, there’s room for improvement. All the broadcasters in Breen’s circle want to get better. Yes, even the guy who has called the Finals since the second George W. Bush administration. “Every year I feel like I can get better at something, whether it’s having a more concise call, a better way to put into perspective what it means, the big picture stuff,” Breen says. This is not debatable. An NBA game feels important when Breen calls it. He’s at the point in his career – he’s called the Finals on TV since 2006; he’s been the voice of the Knicks (on radio, then TV) since 1991 – where he’s at the top of his profession. And that’s right: The Knicks, his boyhood team, are defending world champs after 53 years , thanks to a title run down a volcano, through a black hole, and over a rainbow. It’s all happening! The ego is in check. After all, there are so many voices. Breen did not have to talk to another media meatball after calling a Sixers-Pacers game the night before and hopping on a plane. During a 40-minute phone conversation in late October, the Fordham alumnus and “Bang!” enthusiast discussed the early part of his season, whether he cried after Game 5, and why his enthusiasm for the job has not waned. This interview was condensed for clarity and length. Have you rounded into form yet? That’s a good question. It usually takes me anywhere from 10 to 15 games before I feel like I’m in a real rhythm. I know that sounds odd with all the years I’ve done it, but once the NBA season ends, I’m off for pretty much four months. And I think my voice needs to round into form. And just the overall rhythm of getting back into the game and working with your partners, whether it’s on MSG with Clyde (Frazier) or whether it’s on ESPN with “Legs” [Tim Legler] and Richard (Jefferson). I don’t know if there’s any[thing] tangible: OK, I’m doing it this way now. It’s just more of a feel. The voice has to go through a bunch of games and highs and lows and high-intensity moments. There’s been a lot of changes with ESPN’s NBA crew in recent years. What kind of comfort level are you at now with Tim and Richard? Oh, it’s been wonderful. Last year, we worked almost every game together. In past years, they would kind of split up crews just to make schedules work and have everybody get the amount of games they’re supposed to do. But they made it a point to make sure we worked every game together going into the playoffs. So, by playoff time, we had a nice chemistry . I couldn’t be more pleased with how we came along. sports.title: New Zealand Rugby gives strong backing to Dave Rennie after record All Blacks defeat to England
sports.description: New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has given its unequivocal backing to All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie through to the World Cup after back-to-back defeats to Wales and England. The tourists were stunned in Cardiff as Wales beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years, before suffering a record loss to England at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium on Saturday. Rennie was only appointed as Scott Robertson’s successor in March and took charge ahead of the Nations Championship in July, but has now suffered five defeats this year – including three to South Africa during the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour. NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster is clear, though, that the head coach retains their strong backing as the All Blacks prepare to meet England again this weekend. “We have complete confidence in Rens,” Lancaster said. “His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change. “He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment. “He is a very strong head coach. He provides absolute clarity to his team about how they want to play and absolute accountability about what is expected, what is measured. There are no gaps in information or understanding about the environment. The team love him. They are all behind him. They are all happy in the environment. The All Blacks suffered a record defeat to England (Getty) “Rens has incredible attention to detail. If you talk to Rens about the game he wants to play, he backs it all up by facts, evidence and data. Nothing is left to chance. Nothing is done on gut feel or assumption. He is in our mind the right man to take this team to the World Cup.” Rennie made a strong start to his tenure, beating France, Italy and Ireland in July before conquering the Springboks at Ellis Park in the first of a four-Test series. Two thrashings of Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup in October and Scotland were beaten in their November opener, but the head coach admitted his side “let the country down” after the Wales defeat. The squad have had to deal with the sudden passing of security chief Logan Cadwallader in Edinburgh, which is understood to have hit them hard, while the demands of a gruelling year of international action have also perhaps been felt. It is thought that both the All Blacks and South Africa will consider the impacts of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series , which also included four non-capped tour games, ahead of the next edition on New Zealand soil in 2030. As regards Rennie’s future, Lancaster intends to make it clear after next year’s Rugby Championship – which will feature a full schedule against Australia, the Springboks and Argentina. “Our intention is to make all those decisions before we go into the World Cup. sports.description: MILWAUKEE, WI - OCTOBER 11: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts after pitching in the first inning during Game One of the National League Championship Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Sunday, October 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images In case you have not heard the news yet, Tarik Skubal is a New York Met. You are likely going to be hearing a lot more about this over the coming weeks, especially with a looking lockout that could stretch into the season, robbing us of some extra time with Skubal (don’t worry about that, because he is also here for nine years). The Mets’ biggest need heading into the offseason was their starting rotation, and they addressed that by landing the biggest free agent not just at the position but in the entire sport. In doing so, the club added a two-time Cy Young Award winner who will immediately slot into the No. 1 spot in their rotation and give them the true ace they’ve been sorely lacking, arguably since Jacob deGrom left for Texas following the 2022 season. Skubal, who turned 30 years old on November 20, is coming off something of a down year, by his standards. He posted a 2.72 ERA, a 2.51 FIP, and 186 strikeouts in 158 2/3 innings across 26 starts. He started the year with the Tigers before heading over to the Dodgers and the year with 4.3 bWAR. He also pitched in two postseason games for Los Angeles and allowed three earned runs in 11 innings while striking out 14. Again, I would like to heavily stress that those numbers are pedestrian by his standards, and mostly because of what he did the previous two years in Detroit. In 2024, he finished with the best ERA (2.39), FIP (2.49), and bWAR (6.7) in the AL while leading the league in wins (18) and strikeouts (228). Unsurprisingly, he was a unanimous Cy Young winner while placing seventh in AL MVP voting. He followed that up by leading the AL (again) in ERA (2.21), FIP (2.45), and bWAR (6.4) while finishing with the best WHIP (0.89) and BB/9 (1.5) in the league en route to a second consecutive Cy Young Award (albeit not unanimous this time) and a fifth-place finish in AL MVP voting. So Skubal is set as the ace of the rotation, but where do the Mets go beyond the left-hander? sports.description: COLUMBIA, MO - NOVEMBER 21: Missouri Tigers safety Santana Banner (15) celebrates with teammates after intercepting the pass sealing his teams win during a SEC conference game between the Kentucky Wildcats and the Missouri Tigers held on Saturday November 21, 2026 at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium in Columbia MO. (Photo by Rick Ulreich/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the key matchups between the Bluegrass State and Show-Me State this past Saturday night was Mizzou safety Santana Banner and preseason All-SEC tight end Willie Rodriguez. Banner, playing the STAR position, came in as Mizzou’s second-leading tackler, trailing Nicholas Rodriguez, while Willie Rodriguez has risen to be one of the better pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. Only Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers has more receiving yards among SEC tight ends. A sequence of plays on Saturday by Banner helped propel Mizzou to a 28-14 victory over No. 16 Kentucky, dropping the visitors’ playoff odds to 0.1%. Early in the third quarter, facing a second-and-goal, Banner matched up man-to-man in the slot with Rodriguez. Kenny Minchey didn’t hesitate on who he was going to in the end zone. His head turned right to his 6-foot-4 tight end. The ball was placed right into the numbers of Rodriguez, but the long arms of Banner prevented what could have been an 8-yard score. On the next play, third and goal, Minchey, under pressure from a cover-0 blitz, threw the ball behind Brock Coffman, but the sophomore wide receiver was blanketed by none other than Banner. Kentucky had to settle for a field goal, making it 21-6, instead of a one possession ballgame. Not allowing touchdowns in the red zone proved important for the Tigers. On the night, Kentucky reached Mizzou’s red zone seven times, but mustered just one touchdown in a two-possession loss. Banner himself, and we’ll get more into his statistics in a bit, was one of the catalysts in the Tigers’ defense responding after a poor performance against Georgia and Texas. “We played to our standard,” said Banner after Mizzou’s seventh win on the year. “Something we haven’t done the last couple of weeks.” Banner put the game on ice in another man-to-man coverage rep on Rodriguez in the fourth quarter with Mizzou up 28-14 with under three to play. sports.title: Eric Kjar’s First Season at Weber State Continues into Playoffs
sports.description: BOULDER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 12: Head Coach Eric Kjar of the Weber State Wildcats walks the field during the second quarter against the Colorado Buffaloes at Folsom Field on September 12, 2026 in Boulder, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Weber State had high hopes when it hired Eric Kjar to be its newest football coach following last season. In 2025 the Wildcats won just four games and made a coaching change in the middle of the season, relieving former head man Micky Mental of his duties in early November. Kjar came in over the offseason from the high school ranks, having coached at Corner Canyon High School. His successes were unparalleled in Draper as he went 112-10 with six state championships over the last nine seasons. That success, as Weber State hoped it might, has certainly spilled over in his first season at the helm in Ogden. Kjar’s team went 8-4 this fall and, as of Sunday, found out they’ll keep on playing. For the first time since 2022, Weber State is back in the FCS playoffs as an at-large selection out of the Big Sky and on top of that they get to host. Western Illinois comes to town this weekend and, with them, the chance to turn an already great first year for Kjar into a fantastic one with a win. Weber State made some real noise in the Big Sky this year. Whether it was the big Week 7 win over Idaho State or taking Montana State down to the wire the following week or taking down ranked UC Davis and Northern Arizona in back-to-back games over the last month, the Wildcats certainly did enough to earn their way into the postseason. It was a multitude of things that clicked well for them along the way but one of the biggest was the addition of game changers to the roster, starting with standout freshman quarterback Nate Dahle. Kjar and his staff brought Dahle in from Ridgeway High School in Millville, Utah and he’s been terrific. Dahle has thrown for over 2,500 yards and 25 touchdowns this season. He’s been the spark for an offense that was lacking one in recent years. Alongside Dahle has been the resurgance of Noah Kjar. The son of Kjar himself, Noah has actually been with the team for three years now but was sidelined for much of last season with an injury. Now with his father calling the shots, Kjar has come alive again for the WSU offense, hauling in 79 passes for 1,179 yards and 14 scores. sports.title: The secret injury clause that has Bayern Munich freaking out over Jamal Musiala
sports.description: (Photo by S. Mellar/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Talk about a masterclass in negotiation. When Bayern Munich signed Jamal Musiala onto a bumper contract in 2025, there was speculation surrounding the details. Most drew attention to his salary increase, but a certain secret clause inserted by the player’s camp now has FC Bayern in a bind. According to a report by Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ), Jamal Musiala has a special guarantee in his contract that allows him to earn his full salary for six months in the event of an injury. With the emerging revelations about Musiala’s neurological issues, this clause has become a major sticking point for FC Bayern. Why does this matter? Most people don’t know this, but when a player gets injured playing in the Bundesliga, the club only has to pay six weeks of guaranteed salary before insurance takes over. So, if Musiala were to miss more than six weeks, Bayern Munich would have been off the hook. If it was a regular contract. Instead, with this clause, Musiala is guaranteed to be paid his substantial wages for up to half a year in the event of illness or injury. This means that, if Musiala experiences another episode and misses several months of football, he would still cost the club millions of euros despite not being able to contribute on the pitch. This is not the first time a clause like this has been granted by FC Bayern. Manuel Neuer also had something similar in his previous contracts, and Alphonso Davies is rumored to have one as well (though for a shorter duration of 3-4 months). For Musiala, the clause is doing what it’s supposed to. It is giving the player a semblance of security during this uncertain period in his life. For Bayern, however, it is turning into a massive liability. This may go some ways to explain the strange behavior by the executive team in recent days, though it is unlikely to win them any sympathy. With so many millions of euros on the line, and Musiala’s contract running to 2030, Bayern Munich are in desperate need of a solution to a problem they agreed to have. Join the conversation! technology.title: British retailer Next downplays data breach at tech supplier
technology.description: British retailer Next has become the latest high street name to find itself caught up in a cyberattack, although it insists the data accessed by hackers is "benign" and its customers have nothing to worry about. The clothing and homeware giant told investors on Monday that a third-party supplier had suffered a security breach, allowing an unauthorized party to access information relating to Next. The retailer says its own systems remain untouched and that, so far, there's no evidence that customer personal data has fallen into the wrong hands. "We have been informed that one of our third-party online suppliers has experienced a cyber incident which has resulted in unauthorized access to certain benign data relating to NEXT," the company said in its statement, which it shared with The Register . "We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier." The breached supplier provides technology services to Next, and the "benign" information accessed is understood to be low-level data. Sensitive customer details, including addresses, passwords, and banking information, are believed to be unaffected. Next hasn't identified the supplier, explained exactly what the hackers managed to get their hands on, or revealed how much information was accessed, and declined to say when asked by The Register . However, the retailer has seemingly decided that the stolen data won’t be of much use to the criminals responsible. "Our investigations are ongoing; however, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised," Next said. "The information affected is limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or NEXT." Next also stressed that its own IT infrastructure had escaped unscathed, saying it was "confident that NEXT’s own systems have not been compromised and that this remains an incident affecting the supplier's environment." Despite repeatedly describing the compromised information as harmless, Next says it is treating the incident "with the utmost seriousness" and is working with the affected supplier, law enforcement, and relevant regulators. The incident comes just weeks after fellow British fashion retailer Asos suffered a breach of its own , with hackers gaining access to customer information through third-party platforms. That attack, which came to light on October 6 when customers received an unauthorized push notification through the Asos app announcing that the company had been hacked, was traced to a social engineering scam. An attacker impersonated a trusted contact to trick an Asos employee into handing over login credentials, which were then used to access external platforms. Asos later admitted that the intruders had accessed customer names, contact details, and some account information, but passwords and payment card details were apparently off limits. technology.description: There's no telling what caused the Nvidia board to unanimously vote to reinstate Huang less than a week after saying his return wasn’t under consideration - except reportedly the threat of having one's head ripped off and brain peed on - but that really doesn't matter, at least as far as shareholders need to be concerned: Jensen's back in charge and all’s right in the world of chip stocks. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said of the decision to reinstate him, calling it an honor. Nvidia kicked its former-cum-current CEO and president to the curb on November 12, but not over allegations that he may have been sleeping with a suspected Chinese spy - it was affairs at Nvidia with his subordinates that appears to have been the last straw with Nvidia directors. Nvidia stock has tumbled since Huang’s ouster, and much of the rest of the tech stock world followed suit . Nvidia insiders and tech heavyweights have been pushing for Huang’s return for about as long as he was unemployed, but calls for his return from the US federal government may have been the catalyst for a change of heart among Nvidia leadership who didn’t want Huang back. "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk," Nvidia said in its statement announcing Huang’s return. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," board chair Harvey Jones added. Jones was made Nvidia's first board chair upon Huang’s resignation, and will remain in that role. It's not clear what senior levels of the US government weighed in on Huang's return, but President Donald Trump opined that the company had made "the correct and proper decision" in welcoming Huang back. "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security," Trump said in a post on Truth Social. "The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." ®

The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing. The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly , leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor. Trump went on to say that "we're not going to allow our companies to build datacenters outside of our country," adding that "they allowed that to happen with chips and everything else and it was very destructive to our country." The threat appeared to catch even his own administration unbriefed. "I haven't even said that to my people, but I'm telling them now," Trump said. Trump said: "We're not going to allow companies to build datacenters in other countries. If they do that, they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them. We want them to do it here." technology.description: A recent update broke attachment handling for some New Outlook users, prompting Microsoft to recommend switching to the web or Classic version of its email client. Things are going swimmingly for New Outlook, the email client that Microsoft would very much like users to migrate to. A code change meant that for some users, opening or uploading email attachments failed. It took the company two attempts to fix the problem. Microsoft confirmed there were issues on November 20, as reports that customers were having problems with attachments began rolling in. By the end of the day, the company had added inline images in email to the litany of woe and "paused the rollout of a recent client update that may be contributing to attachment failures." The advice for affected users was to switch to the web version, or use Outlook Classic to open or upload attachments and view inline images. The good news was that Microsoft produced a fix. The bad news was that this fix only resolved problems with Office attachments and inline images, leaving other attachment types affected, according to incident notice EX1561765. The Windows behemoth tried again with a "supplemental fix" and reported the remaining problems resolved on November 21. Users needed to close and reopen New Outlook for the fix to take effect. Microsoft said it had tested the fixes before deployment. Administrators might reasonably wish the original update had received the same attention. The preliminary root cause was a "recent update to the code which supports embedded web content unexpectedly caused impact." The clock is ticking for Outlook Classic. Microsoft is clear that New Outlook is the future, though Classic Outlook will remain available until at least 2029. The fact that the company had to suggest that affected users fall back on the old warhorse to perform that rarely used email activity – attachment handling – is less than confidence-inspiring. Still, by the time Outlook Classic is finally put out to pasture, we're sure Microsoft's habit of sending out broken updates will also be a thing of the past. Right? ®
